record.paper_title: Physical Layer Security in Satellite Communication: State-of-the-art and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can physical-layer security techniques be designed for satellite communication systems to preserve availability against denial-of-service and jamming attacks, given that satellites and satellite links can be overwhelmed by malicious traffic and can be targeted by multiple forms of jamming that distort signals and prevent correct decoding and processing, and given that any proposed method must remain feasible under the unique physical characteristics of satellite communication?

evidence.quote: Satellite systems can suffer denial of service attacks if the satellite or link is overwhelmed with malicious packets that the satellite cannot handle and cause service outages for legitimate users. Moreover, anti-jamming techniques for satellite communications need to be investigated since it is a wireless signal that adversaries can target through multiple types of jamming, causing transformations to the signals that prevent correct decoding and processing.
Therefore, more works should consider PLS availability techniques in satellite scenarios to study its feasibility with the unique physical characteristics of satellite communication.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a satellite communication system modeled as follows. A legitimate transmitter T (a ground station or satellite) communicates with a legitimate receiver R over a wireless channel whose physical characteristics include: (i) very large propagation distances (LEO, MEO, or GEO orbits) producing severe path loss and propagation delays, (ii) high relative motion inducing Doppler shifts, (iii) limited on-board power and processing resources at the satellite, (iv) broad-beam coverage so that any geographic adversary within the footprint can receive and transmit on the same band, and (v) shared spectrum subject to atmospheric and ionospheric impairments. An adversary class A is allowed to mount two types of availability attacks:

(a) Denial-of-service flooding: A injects high-rate malicious traffic toward T or R such that the legitimate processing/queueing capacity is exceeded with probability at least p_DoS.

(b) Jamming: A emits interference signals (constant, pulsed, sweep, tone, protocol-aware, or smart/reactive jamming) of total average power up to P_J and arbitrary waveform structure within the system bandwidth W, with the goal of preventing correct decoding at R.

Design a physical-layer security (PLS) scheme—i.e., a transmission strategy specifying signal design, coding, beamforming, frequency/time hopping, power control, and/or admission control performed at the physical layer (without relying on cryptographic upper-layer mechanisms)—that achieves the following availability guarantee: for every admissible adversary strategy of types (a) and (b), the probability that R correctly decodes each transmitted message is at least 1 − ε, while the scheme remains implementable under the satellite physical constraints (i)–(v) (in particular, bounded on-board energy E, antenna aperture, and computational complexity polynomial in the block length).

The problem is: provide such a PLS construction together with a rigorous proof of its availability guarantee, or establish fundamental impossibility bounds (in terms of W, P_J, E, p_DoS, ε) showing the regimes in which no such scheme can exist.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction concerning PLS availability and anti-jamming in satellite communications. Recent surveys (2023–2025) continue to list anti-jamming and DoS-resilient PLS for satellite/LEO systems as open problems, with various partial schemes (e.g., spread-spectrum hopping, beam-nulling, NOMA-based jamming mitigation) proposed but no general solution under realistic satellite constraints.

status_evidence.title: Physical Layer Security for Satellite Communications: Techniques, Challenges, and Open Issues
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys anti-jamming and availability-oriented PLS for satellite links and explicitly lists them among open research challenges.
status_evidence.claim: Availability and anti-jamming PLS for satellite communications remains an open research area.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on Physical Layer Security for 5G/6G Communications over Satellite
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies DoS resilience and anti-jamming PLS designs adapted to satellite physical constraints as ongoing open problems.
status_evidence.claim: No general PLS scheme guaranteeing availability under arbitrary jamming and DoS in satellite settings has been established.
